result:
I like the hour when the house is quiet but not asleep. The fridge hums. A car passes two streets over and the sound thins out like someone turning down a radio. 

I make tea and don't drink it right away. I just hold the mug and watch the steam make a little ghost of my face in the air. It’s warm on my palms and I think about how many things in life are just about being held for a little while before they’re gone.

There’s a plant on the windowsill that I keep forgetting to name. It’s doing fine without a name. It leans toward the light in the morning and then just exists. I think I should be more like that plant. Less narrating, more leaning.

Sometimes I walk around the block with no destination. I notice how the same street looks completely different if you’re not trying to get anywhere. The cracks in the sidewalk become maps. A kid’s chalk drawing of a dinosaur is half-washed away by rain, and it’s still beautiful because someone cared enough to draw it there.

I think people underestimate small kindnesses. Holding a door. Saying “I’m proud of you” to someone who didn’t ask for it. Leaving the last cookie. They’re tiny, but they’re how the world stays soft.

If I could tell you one thing, it would be this: pay attention to the in-between moments. The waiting for the kettle. The pause before a song starts. The breath you take before you say something true. That’s where most of the life is hiding.

Anyway. It’s getting late. The tea is finally cool enough to drink.
